fields.headline: Trip the cell room?
fields.narration: All hands, this is Darnell Hughes, Incident Commander. The SIS logic was changed without approval and the key switch is in PROGRAM. Until the logic is validated, the SIS cannot be trusted anywhere in the plant. Unit 100 is still making chlorine and the scrubber C-650 can take the full cell-room output for about 40 minutes. Do we trip the cell room now with SIF-110 out of trust, by tripping the rectifiers locally, and accept an 18 to 24 hour restart and membrane damage, or keep Unit 100 running with Unit 300 stopped and the hand valves manned?
keyFacts: SIS logic was changed without an MOC; the key switch is in PROGRAM
Unit 100 is still making chlorine; Unit 300 is stopped
Scrubber C-650 can take the full cell-room output for about 40 minutes
A cell-room restart takes 18 to 24 hours and can damage the membranes
fields.expectedAction: Operations Section Chief and IC decide (ERP 6.3, decision record ERP-D3); the OT Engineer states which safety functions can no longer be relied on; the decision and its rationale are recorded.

fields.headline: SIS Integrity Compromised — Manual Closure Decision
fields.narration: All hands, this is Darnell Hughes, Incident Commander. We have confirmation: the control system was manipulated. The SIS logic was changed without approval. The key switch was left in PROGRAM mode. The ERT is in Level A suits and ready to close HV-312. I need a decision: do we keep automation and risk another wrong command, or do we take ESD-310 offline and manually close HV-312?
keyFacts: SIS logic was changed without an MOC
Triconex key switch is in PROGRAM mode
ERT is on-site and in Level A suits
HV-312 is still open and releasing chlorine
Field observation overrides screen data per C5 and C4
fields.expectedAction: IC calls for a high-consequence decision. The OT Engineer must respond with a clear rationale based on SIS integrity and field authority. The Shift Supervisor must prepare to issue the manual order.
